name: [D1] Persist stop and state-failure outcomes before relaunch (M)
description:
Persist stop and state-failure outcomes before relaunch

Location: src/ovcaq/runtime/supervisor.py; src/ovcaq/runtime/session.py; src/ovcaq/state/commands.py; tests/runtime/test_supervisor.py; tests/runtime/test_supervisor_process.py; tests/packaging/test_installed_supervisor_cli.py

Reuse: existing StateStore/StateService, pure decisions, shared runtime ownership and test fixtures.

Contract (source requirement/design excerpts):
- stop is an immediate process signal plus a supervisor-authored state outcome;
- state-write failure is a supervisor error when possible; the only last-resort
  side channel is an emergency file written when the store cannot function.

Details:
Integrate the existing record_state_failure path for supervisor state read/write failures: attempt a sanitized durable notice through the state writer and fall back to its emergency record only when that write fails. Check existing emergency evidence before capability reconciliation or other supervisor mutations. Ensure a subsequent run cannot relaunch until the existing acknowledgement/recovery path resolves the recorded failure. On SIGTERM/SIGINT and ovcaq stop, retain an explicit stopped outcome in existing control fields when the store works, in addition to summary/metric evidence: set control.pause_requested=true and control.pause_reason to a Notice with site=operator_stop, detail naming the signal number, and created_at from the injected clock. Preserve a pre-existing phase-level pause reason, control.attention, recovery intent, and drained results; never replace a review-cap recovery key. Use the same state-failure path if publication fails. This conservative stop intent requires the existing boundary resume command before another launch. Preserve immediate owned-process cleanup and shell exit statuses. Exercise real subprocess stop and post-failure restart gates, not just manually preseeded emergency files.

### Findings (verbatim)
- 🟡 `record_state_failure` has no production caller. Supervisor state read/write failures return HALT without emergency evidence, so the `require_no_emergency_failure` gate never fires for a real failure and the next `ovcaq run` relaunches (plan §8.4) | File: src/ovcaq/runtime/supervisor.py:583 | Consensus: [1/3]
- ⚪ `Supervisor.run` reconciles capabilities (a state write) before `require_no_emergency_failure`, so it writes state before checking whether the store was declared broken | File: src/ovcaq/runtime/supervisor.py:142 | Consensus: [1/3]
- 🟡 `ovcaq stop` leaves no durable stopped outcome in state. The SIGTERM path only finalizes summary.json and the metric (`decision="halt"`), but plan §6 and §8.4 require "record the stopped outcome" as a supervisor-authored state outcome | File: src/ovcaq/runtime/supervisor.py:138 | Consensus: [1/3]

Acceptance criteria:
- Every quoted finding no longer reproduces.
- Every decision is explainable from committed state plus summary.
- Metrics, pause, stop, retry, park, and halt contracts pass.
- Required post-drain capability lifecycle and independent retry pass.

Verify: tests fail for the quoted regression before implementation and pass after; run applicable focused tests, source quality gates, and the work skill's mandatory final verification. Do not read live launcher homes in tests.
